issues.title: Amplitude objective is undefined for potentially negative noisy data

issues.failure_explanation: The proof establishes at most the forward implication from equality to stationarity and never proves the converse. The converse is false: with one scalar region, \(Q=1\), \(d=1\), and \(z^{(0)}=2\), exact surrogate minimization gives \(z^{(1)}=1\). Then \(\nabla\Phi(z^{(1)})=0\), while \(\Phi(z^{(1)})=0<1/2=\Phi(z^{(0)})\).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the biconditional by the one-way implication actually supported, subject also to resolving the differentiability issue at zero coefficients.
issues.overall_effect: The theorem's claimed characterization of stalled iterations by stationarity is false.
issues.title: Stationarity does not imply equality of consecutive objective values
issues.why_classification: A comparable monotonicity theorem survives, but the advertised equivalence and its optimality interpretation must be withdrawn.

issues.failure_explanation: The complex cross terms are mishandled when the proof converts the quadratic expansion into a gradient bound, producing too much guaranteed decrease. A direct counterexample is \(N=1\), \(P=Q=1\), \(d=1\), \(z^{(0)}=2\), and \(n=0\): the left side is \(1\), while the stated right side is \((1/2)\Phi(2)=1/4\).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redo the quadratic descent calculation with the real inner product and replace the constant by one justified by that calculation.
issues.overall_effect: The explicit sublinear bound is false, although an \(O(1/n)\) bound with a weaker constant may remain possible.
issues.title: The convergence-rate bound has an incorrect constant
issues.why_classification: The counterexample only defeats the numerical constant; a local algebraic correction can retain the same stationarity measure and sublinear order.

issues.failure_explanation: A coarse probe entry can vanish by phase cancellation even when its fine-bin intensity is positive. For example, a bin containing \((1,-1,1,-1)\) has \(Q_H=0\) and \(I_h^H|Q|^2=1\), hence \(W_u^H=0\) and \(u_H=0\). At the coarsest recursive update the denominator \(u_H+|Q_H|^2\) is then zero, so the algorithm evaluates \(0/0\).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Introduce a strictly positive coarse regularization or a cancellation-safe coarse-probe construction, and then rederive the coarse update, descent result, and parameter-transfer rule.
issues.overall_effect: MGPS and therefore MGrPIE are not well-defined for ordinary complex probes whose values cancel under averaging; the claimed coarse update and automatic regularization guarantee also fail there.
issues.title: Phase cancellation makes the recursive multigrid solver singular
issues.why_classification: A contained redesign can plausibly preserve the multigrid architecture, but merely editing a degenerate case is insufficient because the chosen automatic regularization deliberately becomes zero.

These are generally unequal when the fine-grid denominators vary within a bin. None of the cited replication lemmas permits a nonlinear reciprocal to commute with averaging.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redesign the coarse regularization using the relevant harmonic average, or weaken the claim to a valid inequality and analyze the resulting stability.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed equality of worst-case fine and coarse update magnitudes, and hence the advertised automatic transfer of regularization, is unsupported even away from singular coarse probes.

issues.why_classification: Repair requires changing or reanalyzing the coarse parameter rule, but it remains a contained part of the multigrid construction.

issues.overall_effect: The proposition's claimed strictness and stationarity characterization of the coarse correction are false, although its nonpositivity conclusion can remain valid.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: gives a descending direction of the surrogate model on the fine grid

issues.failure_explanation: The formal multigrid result proves only that the coarse correction is a descent direction at one point. The algorithm takes that direction with unit step, without a line search or a bound ensuring actual decrease, and then performs sequential stochastic updates with changing surrogate centers. No theorem establishes monotonic descent or convergence for MGPS/MGrPIE; the monotonicity and rate theorems concern exact full surrogate minimization in \(\eqref{eqn:surrogate_minimization}\), not the proposed stochastic multigrid algorithm.
